articles.headline: Here's how both the Giants and the Commanders turned a likely victory into a tie
keyFacts: The New York Giants and Washington Commanders tied 27-27 after both teams failed to attempt game-winning overtime field goals.
Cam Skattebo lost a fumble and Jayden Daniels was tackled before spiking the ball, preventing either team from attempting a field goal.
Giants coach John Harbaugh said the team will probably use the same clock-running strategy next time.
body: LANDOVER Md. (AP) — With the game tied at 27, the Washington Commanders and New York Giants each had chances to run the clock down and kick a routine field goal to win in overtime. Here's a recap — call it an oral history of misery — of how each team blew it on Sunday.
2 minutes remaining, the Giants are seemingly in control

It was first-and-10 from the Washington 24. Since it was the third possession of overtime, this was a sudden-death situation. The Giants could have kicked a field goal right then, but Dominic Zvada had already missed from 50, 57 and 46 yards — and New York coach John Harbaugh's tenure in Baltimore ended last season on a missed field goal from 44 yards.
“That field goal is very makeable, but it's not a gimme,” Harbaugh said. “I've had some experience with that.”

So the plan was to try to advance a little bit closer while also running more time off the clock. The Commanders were out of timeouts — remember that for later — and the Giants could have run so much time off that even if Zvada missed again, Washington would have had no chance to drive the other way and the game would end in a tie.
“That's the strategy we'll probably do next time, too,” Harbaugh said.
Skattebo fumbles, giving Washington a lifeline

The Giants could have run the clock down by simply taking a knee a couple of times. Instead, Cam Skattebo took a handoff and was met behind the line of scrimmage. Washington's Daron Payne knocked the ball loose and Shy Tuttle recovered for the Commanders.
“There's 11 guys on the other team just screaming at you,” Skattebo said. “Telling you you messed up, it's your fault, you sold the game, everything. You get that.”
55 seconds left, Washington in field goal range

Two passes and a run had the Commanders across midfield. Then Jayden Daniels threw a pass to Treylon Burks, who went out of bounds with 55 seconds left. It was now first-and-10 from the New York 26. Washington was in the same position the Giants had just squandered — with a chance to run the clock down and try a field goal for the win on the final play.
“Defense did a great job of getting a stop and forcing the turnover,” Daniels said. “At that point, it was like, OK, we got to go win this football game.”
Rachaad White ran the ball 2 yards to the New York 24 — and the clock started ticking.
27 seconds left, the Commanders are in no rush

Once the clock was under 40 seconds, Washington could have taken a knee, let the time run all the way down and then had Daniels spike the ball with under 5 seconds remaining. Instead, the Commanders went into a huddle, and with 27 seconds to go they were still in it.
The plan was apparently to throw the ball — to someone who could easily get out of bounds. If need be, Daniels could always toss the ball away for a clock-stopping incompletion.
“It’s an outside throw or a clock — an out-of-bounds throw, or a clock,” coach Dan Quinn said.
13 seconds left, Washington finally snaps the ball

The Commanders broke the huddle and Daniels lined up under center. Someone even went in motion. By the time the play began, the Commanders could not risk having someone tackled in bounds, because the clock could run out.
“We have to stop the clock. We have to know the situation,” Daniels said. “We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me.”
8 seconds left, Daniels is tackled

After the snap, Daniels rolled to his left and Ben Sinnott ran a route toward the sideline. Instead of throwing, Daniels turned inside and was tackled. It's still not clear if he knew Washington was out of timeouts.
“We just got to communicate that,” he said. “That's the whole thing. As I said, it starts with me communicating to the whole offense in the huddle, and I think everyone will say that top down.”
3 seconds left, Commanders in chaos

Washington's fate might have been sealed the moment Daniels was tackled, but the clock would still have stopped if the Commanders could have lined up legally and had the quarterback spike the ball before it expired. It's hard to say how many players realized exactly what the situation was.

Daniels stayed down for a couple seconds, looking around. Tackle Josh Conerly Jr. started making a bit of a spiking motion with his hand as if to tell Daniels what was needed. Sinnett headed back toward the line of scrimmage with nowhere near enough urgency. New York edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux stood with his hands on his hips.
Tight end John Bates lined up out wide to the far side, motioning to hurry up.
“The right call is honestly like we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot,” Quinn said. “That is my responsibility.”
No time left: Giants 27, Commanders 27

The clock ran out. Defensive lineman Shelby Harris started waving both arms to indicate the game should be over. Cornerback Deonte Banks leaped in the air, ran across the line of scrimmage, then leaped again in celebration. Quinn ripped off his headset and threw it to the ground.
A tie snatched first from the jaws of victory and then from the jaws of defeat.
“I wanted to get off the field before they could take it away from us, I guess,” Harbaugh said. “I was surprised. I can't say that I wasn't. It was a pretty shocking end there.”
And for Skattebo, relief.
“I probably won't get reamed as much,” he said. “But I'm still going to get reamed.”

articles.headline: Fantasy Football Booms & Busts: Packers have a big day as Bears blow it in Week 5
keyFacts: The Green Bay Packers defeated the Chicago Bears 31-7 in Week 5 behind 428 yards of total offense.
Packers quarterback Jordan Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns.
Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams might return for the team's Week 6 game against Atlanta.
body: It feels like a golden age for head coaches in the NFC North. Ben Johnson is the offensive genius for the Bears. Dan Campbell is the culture-changer and the fourth-down guy in Detroit. It's almost mandatory to call Minnesota's Kevin O'Connell a quarterback whisperer on every first reference, though that label might be getting a little stale.
Matt LaFleur? Oh, he's the guy in Green Bay who makes the playoffs just about every year and yet somehow stays on the hot seat most of the time.

So it had to be satisfying for LaFleur to roll over Johnson and the Bears on Sunday, 31-7. The Packers collected 428 yards of offense (Chicago managed just 246) and were never challenged in the game. Green Bay cranked out 7.3 yards per play, while the Bears sputtered to just 3.8 per snap.

All of the primary Green Bay fantasy angles came home, especially the pieces in the passing game. Quarterback Jordan Love had a near-perfect day, completing 25-of-31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns. The Packers hit on six long passes for the game, including two home-run touchdowns to Christian Watson (6-143-2). Matthew Golden didn't score a TD, but he still got loose for 6-123-0, plus a two-point conversion catch. Tucker Kraft caught all five of his targets for 64 yards, one of them a 46-yard rainbow down the right sideline.

Say this for Love, he knows where his bread was buttered. His Big 3 accounted for 330 of Green Bay's 367 receiving yards. A narrow target tree is a fantasy manager's best friend. And the Packers might need to throw even more aggressively in future weeks, because there are still plenty of questions about the Green Bay defense (Chicago's backup QBs didn't provide much of a test Sunday).

We also should note the Packers still aren't running well on the ground (2.7 YPC), though MarShawn Lloyd bailed out his day with two rushing touchdowns. LaFleur keeps scratching around for a possible answer — Lloyd had 10 carries, Kaleb Johnson had seven, Pierre Strong had five. Sometimes there are no right answers. Green Bay might have to junk the running game to keep up with the Cowboys and Lions the next two weeks.

Maybe Johnson outsmarted himself by going back to Tyson Bagent. Chicago's presumed No. 2 QB looked lost against the Packers, managing just 4.1 yards per attempt and throwing two picks. He was mercifully benched for Case Keenum in the fourth period, though Keenum was marginally better (5.7 YPA, one pick, no points). The Bears are desperate to get Caleb Williams back; he might be in play for Week 6's game with Atlanta.

So far we're all getting crushed on the pass catchers in the Chicago offense. Rome Odunze drew nine targets but they resulted in a meager 3-40-0 line. Luther Burden III (4-47-0) is not paying off his summer buzz. We're going to have some hard discussions about Colston Loveland (2-19-0) this week, with five straight games under expectation. The Williams return can fix some of these problems, but it feels like wishcasting to expect everyone to magically turn their season around.

D'Andre Swift was fine (73 total yards, touchdown) with the backfield essentially to himself. Roschon Johnson picked up five catches, mostly in garbage time. Here's hoping the Bears find some offensive answers in that Falcons game, because the Patriots and Seahawks have challenging defenses after that.
Jaylen Warren marks his territory

The Steelers opened the year with a backfield platoon, mixing Warren with Rico Dowdle. But with Dowdle out with a toe injury, Warren is staking his claim. Warren was doing a little bit of everything before Week 5, and then went ballistic in Sunday's win over the Colts.

Warren raced to 33.8 fantasy points mostly through distance — he scored on an 80-yard touchdown catch and a 50-yard touchdown run. Aaron Rodgers loves to throw to his backs, and Warren ultimately had a snappy 6-80-1 day through the air. That makes it 19 catches on 26 targets for Warren, on pace for about 65 receptions.
Dowdle is a good player ticketed for some kind of a role eventually, but we have to assume Warren has the lead in Pittsburgh.

We'll spend time handicapping the backs in Pittsburgh, but maybe the receivers are all dead ends. Trendy sleeper Roman Wilson was erased by a finger injury. DK Metcalf (3-12-0, four targets) was invisible, as he often is. Germie Bernard took advantage of nine targets (6-80-0) but maybe that isn't sustainable. I don't know anyone who is going to chase after tight end Pat Freiermuth (5-44-2), who caught two touchdowns out of nowhere. At least the Steelers only targeted six players on the day.
Drake Maye crushes again

Maye's slump was the talking point of September, but he's crushed everything in his path the last two weeks. His sharp play at Buffalo might have saved New England's season, and he was even better Sunday against the Raiders, throwing for four touchdowns and running in a fifth. Maye's perfect day (11.0 YPA, 150.9 rating) came attached to a number of afterthought pass-catchers — Kyle Williams (3-91-1), DeMario Douglas (4-65-2), Efton Chism (5-57-0), Eli Raridon (5-57-1). Hunter Henry (3-44-1), whom you might have started, had the other score. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs was quiet (1-16-0, three targets).

Rhamondre Stevenson (85 total yards, touchdown) held the fort capably, while TreVeyon Henderson left early with an ankle injury. The Patriots offense could really start cooking when A.J. Brown comes back — that might be possible Week 6 against the Jets.
Other Week 6 Booms (early games)

— For the most part, we should all ignore Jacksonville's 19-17 win over Philadelphia. It was a poorly played and poorly coached three hours of football, for the most part. But if you want to specifically dial up Parker Washington's highlight tape (6-124-2), that's allowed. Washington's ADP kept rising all summer but he's still in place to smash his draft-day ticket. Tight end Brenton Strange (7-68-0) has popped the last couple of weeks.

— It rained in New York and Geno Smith was mediocre all day (6.1 YPA, four sacks). It didn't hurt Garrett Wilson much (7-104-1); sometimes you just have to bet on talent. Braelon Allen lugged the mail in the backfield, a 24-116-1 day of pile-moving and consistent positive runs. Breece Hall isn't expected back in Week 6, so we'll dial up Allen at New England.

— Jameis Winston wasn't sharp in the first half at Washington but he eventually came around — 326 passing yards, three touchdowns, just one turnover, just three sacks. But the most delightful thing about Winston is how he peppered his two best players — Malik Nabers (11-121-1) absorbed a silly 20 targets, and Isaiah Likely (11-94-2) collected 13. With concentration that narrow, this can be a fun offense. It was a disappointing return for Cam Skattebo (71 total yards), who almost lost the game with his overtime fumble. Thankfully for New York, the Commanders made a mess of the final minute and the game ended in a tie.
Other Week 7 Busts (early games)

— This was supposed to be the week Chase Brown got his season cooking, but he was a dud at Miami. His 13 rushes netted just 39 yards; he finished with a modest 60 total yards, he lost a fumble. Worse yet, Samaje Perine (16 touches, 78 total yards) stole a touchdown and made this backfield a 50-50 split. The Bengals probably won't look for major changes, heading into their Week 6 bye with a 3-2 record.

— Deshaun Watson finally took a step back for Cleveland, taking eight sacks against the Jets and managing just 4.7 YPA. The Browns' receivers didn't cover themselves in glory, either — although Isaiah Bond had 74 yards receiving, he dropped a couple of passes. Quinshon Judkins continues to be a bell cow (18 opportunities), but the Cleveland line doesn't open many holes (3.1 YPC). Judkins was wearing a walking boot on his right foot after the game.

articles.headline: Massie sides with Trump’s Russia diesel deal despite fraught relationship
keyFacts: Representative Thomas Massie supported President Donald Trump's decision to allow Russia to sell diesel fuel to the United States.
Several Republican lawmakers opposed the deal, and two representatives said they would sponsor legislation to block Russian oil purchases.
Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to American and global markets.
body: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) expressed support for President Donald Trump’s recent decision to allow Russia to sell diesel fuel to the United States and global markets on Sunday.

The two Republican figures have maintained an adversarial relationship throughout Trump’s second term, particularly over the White House’s handling of the Epstein files, the conflict in Iran, and federal spending. Massie was one of two House Republicans who voted against Trump’s signature legislative achievement, the One Big Beautiful Bill, and similarly stalled a Trump-backed stimulus package during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Massie’s surprising alignment with Trump comes after the deal drew backlash from some Republicans throughout the weekend, as Sens. Susan Collins (R-ME), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), and John Curtis (R-UT) sent a letter to Trump telling him to “reverse course immediately” on Sunday. Former Vice President Mike Pence and conservative commentator Laura Loomer similarly expressed frustration with the deal on Saturday, while Reps. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) and Don Bacon (R-NE) said they would sponsor legislation “to block any and all purchases of Russian oil.”

“In 2022 I voted against Russia sanctions, pointing out that U.S. citizens would suffer from higher prices,” Massie said. “Glad to see Trump came around to that reality this week. We should lift sanctions on all the petroleum products, and on raw metals like copper and aluminum.”

The lame-duck lawmaker’s reelection campaign ended when he lost the primary to Trump-backed former Navy SEAL Ed Gallrein, who won by almost 10 percentage points. Massie’s defeat served as one of many examples of Trump’s endorsement power throughout the spring, as the Kentucky lawmaker spearheaded resistance to the White House alongside Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA).

“Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 tons immediately thereafter,” Trump outlined in the initial announcement on Friday. “Additionally, based on the condition of their Diesel Refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel.”
SIX SENATORS DEMAND TRUMP ‘IMMEDIATELY REVERSE COURSE’ ON RUSSIAN DIESEL DEAL

Trump announced Sunday morning that an “energy ceasefire” had been struck between Russia and Ukraine . Trump has searched for solutions to high energy prices in recent weeks and months as stubborn inflation threatens the GOP’s chances of retaining control of Congress in November’s midterm elections. Trump turned to berating Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky late last week for striking Russian oil refineries, arguing high domestic gas prices are in part due to Ukraine’s targeting of such sites.
Zelensky would later say on Sunday that Russia broke the ceasefire agreement and struck a power plant mere hours after Trump announced the agreement.

articles.headline: The reason the Xbox Series S is so much cheaper than the Series X
keyFacts: The Xbox Series S starts at $500, remaining cheaper than the $750 Xbox Series X despite recent price increases for both consoles.
The Series S costs less because it lacks a disc drive and features less storage, RAM, and processing power than the Series X.
Microsoft plans to start sending alpha Project Helix hardware to developers in 2027 ahead of its next console generation.
body: The reason the Xbox Series S is so much cheaper than the Series X
Both consoles have become more expensive since launch, but the Series S is still relatively affordable.

A console nearly six years into its lifecycle would typically have seen a price drop by this point, but that's not the case for the latest Xbox line. On the contrary, the Xbox Series X and S have seen a price increase in recent months. It's not the only system to see these hikes, either. The PlayStation 5's price went up twice within a year and the Nintendo Switch 2 got a heftier price tag in 2026, largely thanks to the ongoing RAMaggedon crisis driving up component prices.

Despite the price hikes, the Series S maintains a price edge over the Series X, starting at $500. That's a stark difference from the Series X's cheapest $750 model, and means the Series S is tied with the Switch 2 for the most affordable modern console. But why is the Series S so much cheaper than the Series X? It all comes down to hardware.
Why the Series X is more expensive

The most obvious difference between these two is that the Series S is a digital-only device that lacks a disc drive. Though there is a model of the Series X that also lacks a disc drive (which knocks $50 off its price), the hardware of the Series X otherwise remains the same. This lock-in to a solely digital landscape is one of the most defining features between the two, which contributes somewhat to its cheaper price tag.

Under the hood, the Series S is also a less impressive piece of hardware then the Series X. The base model of the Series S offers 512GB of storage, with a 1TB model available for $100 more. Meanwhile, the Series X comes with 1TB of space (there was a 2TB Series X model, but Microsoft discontinued it in 2026). Either model can gain more storage with an expansion card that plugs into the back of the console.

The Series X boasts 12 teraflops of processing power and targets 4K resolution, while the Series S has only 4 teraflops and can go up to 1440p in most games. However, both consoles have the capability for 120 fps. On a more technical level, both consoles utilize a custom AMD Zen 2 CPU, but the Series X CPU is clocked higher, giving it an edge in speed. Both also use an AMD RDNA 2 GPU, but the Series X version has 52 CUs (short for compute units, a measurement of processing power) while the Series S has only 20.

Similarly, the Series X has 16GB of RAM, 10GB of which can operate at 560 GB per second and 6GB that can operate at 336 GB/s. Compared to 10GB RAM in the S, with 8GB of it operating at 224 GB/s and 2GB at 56 GB/s, the Series X has much more complex and capable hardware, contributing to its higher price.
Xbox Series X vs. Series S: Which is better for you?

If you're set on getting an Xbox console, which Series is right for you depends on your gaming style. If you aren't someone who has a collection of physical games, or largely plan to play via Game Pass, the Series S's lack of disc drive probably won't bother you. If you prefer to take advantage of disc-based game sales or just hold a game in your hands, the Series X is the way to go.

The Series S is the more compact choice, not just from the space saved by skipping physical games, but because it's about 60 percent smaller than a Series X. It's much easier to slot a Series S into an entertainment center than its larger sibling.

Game resolution and performance will be lower with a Series S, but depending on the games you play and your tolerances, it might not be a big enough difference to matter. If you don't need to see 4K resolution all the time (the S does support 4K upscaling, just not 4K natively), or play many games that aren't graphically intensive, the Series S might be good enough, especially since it can achieve 120 fps in compatible titles. However, if you're a performance purist who wants the very best, you'll want the Series X.

Alternatively, it's worth waiting until Microsoft's Project Helix family of devices comes out if you'd rather not get a console so many years into its lifecycle. These will almost certainly be more expensive than a Series X or S, and we don't know how big the technical advancements will be between this generation and the next. Microsoft plans to start sending alpha Project Helix hardware to developers in 2027, which likely means at least another year after that before we see the final product released. But if you're willing to be patient, consider saving your money for cutting-edge technology.

articles.headline: Daughters of the American Revolution axes chapter that challenged transgender membership
keyFacts: The Daughters of the American Revolution voted to disband its Texas-based Martha Laird Chapter, citing violations of national bylaws.
The chapter opposed admitting transgender women, but DAR stated the dissolution was due to the misuse of chapter resources for outside advocacy.
Individual members retain their DAR membership and remain free to advocate for bylaw changes through established processes, the organization said.
body: Daughters of the American Revolution axes chapter that challenged transgender membership
By
Fox News
Published Oct. 11, 2026, 7:25 p.m. ET
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) voted Saturday to disband its Martha Laird Chapter in Texas that fought to bar transgender women from joining the historic organization, citing violations of its national bylaws.

In a letter to chapter members, DAR Organizing Secretary General Marguerite Hogan Fritsch announced that the National Board of Management had approved the chapter’s dissolution by a two-thirds majority vote.

“On October 10, 2026, at the meeting of the National Board of Management of the National Society, Daughters of the American Revolution a resolution passed by two-thirds majority vote to disband the Martha Laird Chapter, NSDAR,” Fritsch said in the letter. “The actions of the chapter have been found in violation of Article XIX, Section 4 of the Bylaws of the National Society Daughters of the American Revolution,” the letter continued.
The letter did not identify the specific conduct that constituted a violation or state whether the chapter’s opposition to transgender membership contributed to the decision.

The National Society Daughters of the American Revolution confirmed to Fox News Digital that the organization had voted to disband the local Texas chapter but denied it was due to its views on membership.

“The National Board of Management voted on October 10 to disband the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas after finding that chapter officers had used the chapter’s name, leadership positions, communications, and governance processes to further the goals of a separate advocacy organization,” the group told Fox News Digital. “The Board determined that it was this use of chapter authority and resources – not the views being advocated – that constituted conduct discrediting the National Society under Article XIX, Section 4 of the National Bylaws.”

“The Board’s decision was not based on the chapter’s or its members’ views concerning membership eligibility, their efforts to propose changes to the National Bylaws, or their right to advocate for changes in National Society governance,” the statement continued.

The group noted that at their June 2026 meeting, national members had rejected a resolution to add further membership restrictions. Individual members of the Texas chapter retain their DAR membership and are free to advocate for changes to the National Bylaws through the Society’s established governance processes, the organization said.

The chapter previously challenged DAR leadership’s position on transgender membership, with member Laura McDonald telling Fox News Digital last year that the organization was contradicting its founding mission by recognizing transgender women as eligible members.

“But, then they go on to say that a man who claims he’s a woman is a woman, and therefore he’s eligible for membership. But if you are a man that doesn’t claim to be a woman, you’re not eligible for membership,” McDonald said.

Conservative California superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw told Fox News Digital that women and girls are being told that spaces created to protect their privacy, dignity, and opportunities “no longer belong to them,” including sports, restrooms, locker rooms, and now, according to her, the Daughters of the American Revolution.

“The women of the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas stood their ground. They sought to preserve a definition of “Daughters” based on biological sex and asked for a clear vote. On October 10, national leadership dissolved their chapter,” Shaw said.

“Think about that. Women who stood up for their convictions saw their chapter, with a history dating back to 1942, dissolved. Here is the damning question national leadership needs to answer: Why should women be punished for standing up for the very definition of the organization they belong to?” she added.
Shaw also pointed to similar debates across the country concerning sports and privacy in women’s spaces, and said “this is about more than one chapter.”
“Our daughters deserve a future where they never have to ask permission to stand up for the truth, and where no woman is punished for having the courage to speak it,” Shaw said.

Under DAR’s national bylaws, Article XIX, Section 4 authorizes the National Board of Management to discipline or disband chapters that violate organizational rules or engage in conduct that discredits the DAR.

The dissolution comes nearly three months after Rep. Ben Cline, R-Va., introduced the Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act, which would amend DAR’s congressional charter to restrict membership to biological women.
Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., subsequently introduced companion legislation in the Senate.
“Rather than honoring and preserving a lineage-based organization for women, it has embraced radical gender ideology at the expense of the women it was created to serve,” Cline said.
In September 2024, the Martha Laird Chapter, supported by 11 other chapters, submitted a proposed bylaw amendment defining membership eligibility based on biological sex.

The Center for American Liberty also provided legal assistance to the chapter, challenging DAR leadership’s contention that excluding transgender applicants could jeopardize the organization’s tax-exempt status.
The proposed amendment was rejected by DAR’s National Board of Management in February 2025. McDonald criticized the decision at the time.

“The rejection by the National Board of Management of our proposal to define a woman in our bylaws sadly confirms what we knew all along – that leadership is taking a political stance which is not based on fears of the loss of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status,” McDonald said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

DAR, founded in 1890, previously maintained that its longstanding membership policies allowed women with legally amended birth certificates to join, provided they otherwise met the organization’s genealogical requirements.

articles.headline: How a nightmare week in the NFC East impacts all four head coaches
keyFacts: All four NFC East teams had frustrating Week 5 outcomes, with Philadelphia and Dallas losing while Washington and New York tied.
Commanders coach Dan Quinn and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni publicly took blame for late-game coaching mistakes that cost their teams victories.
The article stated that Nick Sirianni must turn Philadelphia around, while Brian Schottenheimer must reach the playoffs to ease job concerns.
body: Week 5 of the NFL season was not kind to the NFC East, as all four teams in the division had frustrating endings to their games.

After the Dallas Cowboys underwhelmed on Thursday night, the Philadelphia Eagles faltered across the pond in the morning while the New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to a tie in the early afternoon. Overall, each of the four teams experienced maddening moments in their games, leading their fans to wonder what could have been.

Still, the four teams didn't have an equal intensity of frustrations in Week 5. In some cases, the team's had coach admitted after the game to costing them the game, while in others, the Week 5 was just a speed bump in the 2026 season.
With all four NFC East teams leaving much to be desired, here's a breakdown of how each result impacts the four head coaches in the division.
MORE: Grading the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade to the Texans
Dan Quinn, Commanders

While the Commanders didn't lose on Sunday, settling for a tie against the Giants may have put Dan Quinn in a difficult hole. Washington was up two possessions for most of the game but blew a 14-point lead as New York forced overtime with a late rally.

Then, in overtime, the Commanders were in prime position to win the game when the offense bungled the final play of the game, allowing the time on the clock to expire. Instead of getting a chance to kick a field goal and win the game, Washington collected a tie.
The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie https://t.co/WmPp6q5hU0
— NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026
"Leaving tonight with a tie feels like a loss," Quinn said after the game. "The right call is to clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility and nobody else's,"

Quinn's seat is perhaps the hottest among the NFC East head coaches, and giving away a tie in a game the team should've won didn't help. Washington is now 1-3-1 in the division, currently in last place, which is why a win vs. New York would have been so important.
MORE: Dan Quinn left furious by Commanders overtime mistake
Nick Sirianni, Eagles

In the opening game on Sunday in London, the Eagles lost in catastrophic fashion to the Jacksonville Jaguars After taking a one-point lead with just eight seconds left, Philadelphia allowed a big kickoff return to the Jaguars that led to a game-winning Jacksonville field goal.
One of the craziest endings of the year. https://t.co/Wm9hwOjk1U
— NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026
Sirianni took the blame after the game, saying that the kicking team should have sent the ball out of the endzone.

"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game. And that's what I said to our guys," he said. "I [didn't] make the decision that I should make at the end of that game, and I cost us that one. And I put that fully on me."

The final sequence is the talking point, but Sirianni was already under the spotlight for the Eagles' lack of production on offense, which didn't improve on Sunday. While the Eagles probably won't fire Sirianni midseason, he does need to turn things around to quiet the outside noise.
Overall, Sirianni's tough day on Sunday will only anger Philadelphia fans even more.
MORE: Nick Sirianni owns up to Eagles loss to Jaguars
Brian Schottenheimer, Cowboys

The Cowboys were grateful for the NFC East's rough Sunday, as it helped put distance between the team's brutal loss on Thursday night. Brian Schottenheimer's squad lost at home on a short week to the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers and undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, falling to 2-3 in the process.

Schottenheimer hoped new defensive coordinator Christian Parker would help fix a broken defense from 2025, but the unit hasn't been much better this year. Instead, the Cowboys once again face the task of needing their offense to overcome their defensive miscues.

Still, Schottenheimer gets the benefit that the Cowboys do not typically make coaching changes, so his job doesn't appear to be in jeopardy. Jerry Jones last fired a head coach midseason in 2010, and every Cowboys head coach since 2000 got at least three seasons at the helm.

While Schottenheimer still needs to make the playoffs to ease any job concerns, his seat likely not as hot as Quinn's or Sirianni's. Dallas also benefits the most from no team winning on Sunday, as the team could feel like it caught a break.
John Harbaugh, Giants

Harbaugh's status as the Giants head coach is in a different galaxy than his three counterparts. Harbaugh has the Giants in first place in his first season as head coach, and New York fans are thrilled that the team is just competing at a high level.

Even the tie vs. Washington on Sunday shows why the Giants are happy with Harbaugh. New York came back from down two touchdowns to force overtime, and the defense held firm late in the game to secure the tie. While the Giants blew a few chances to score in the extra frame, New York fought its way to get to that point.

Harbaugh is not without his faults, as he has made a few decisions in the first few weeks that he probably wants back. Even with the tie, though, Giants fans are more relieved that they didn't lose on the road to a division rival on Sunday.

articles.headline: PvP pinball is such a good idea I can't believe I haven't played it before
keyFacts: Bumper Bout, a two-player competitive pinball game, was featured at PAX Australia as the final game of the Omegathon tournament.
Players compete to deplete an opponent's five hearts by scoring points, sending attack balls across the screen, and using special abilities.
A demo is available on Steam, and the full game is scheduled to launch on October 29 with online multiplayer.
body: One of the great things about videogame conventions is there are always people up for playing a local multiplayer game, just waiting to be handed controls and thrown into a new experience. Which is how, at PAX Australia over the weekend, I found myself playing a game called Bumper Bout. It immediately impressed me with its concept, and then as I played a few rounds of it, with how it executed that concept.

Bumper Bout is two-player competitive pinball. If you know Puyo Puyo Tetris it's like that, but if you don't then imagine you're playing pinball on one half of the screen while someone else beside you is doing the same, only with the ability to flick balls across the divide. While you're trying to land a skill shot or just frantically deal with the balls already pinging between your flippers, the neighbor casually lobs another problem over the fence and says, "Deal with this. Good luck!"

Bumper Bout had the honor of being chosen as the final game of the Omegathon, the main stage tournament that plays out over the course of PAX, where it was introduced as a game made by someone who thought, "I love pinball, but no one ever dies."

Every time a ball goes down the ballhole you lose a heart, and the first player to lose five hearts loses the round. But scoring points by hitting bumpers and targets earns attack balls that you can zip over to harass your opponent, or store until you get four of them, unlocking your character's ultimate ability—which might let you create a gravity well or, if you're playing the pirate, throw bombs around the already hectic playfield.

Those playfields include a space level where satellites and moons bounce into each other to make even more chaos, and a foosball table where the flippers also activate half the player standees so you can use them to flick balls around as well. It takes a lot to overcome the noise and overwhelm of a busy show floor, but while I was playing Bumper Bout I was fully locked in.

I've seen plenty of demos that are popular at conventions fail to translate that popularity to the final release, but I hope that Bumper Bout can manage it. It's got singleplayer, with arcade and survival modes planned, and the final version will have online multiplayer too. You can try the demo for yourself on Steam, and the full game will be out on October 29.

articles.headline: Terminal in Riyadh airport hit again, a day after deadly strike killed 12
keyFacts: A terminal at Riyadh's international airport was attacked on Sunday, one day after a strike killed at least 12 people.
Yemen's Houthi group claimed responsibility for the airport strikes, describing them as retaliation for Saudi military aggression.
President Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis, as the group threatened additional airport attacks.
body: A passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, was attacked again on Sunday, one day after a on the Riyadh airport killed at least 12 people, including a U.S. citizen, and wounded hundreds of others.
The second attack comes as Yemen's Houthi group said they carried out at least four operations targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh since Saturday.

Saudi authorities said there were injuries in the latest attack on the King Khalid International Airport complex for terminals 3 and 4, serving domestic flights. The airport — struck four times in the past five days — has been closed since Saturday's missile attack, which was the deadliest in a Gulf Arab nation since the Iran war began. Over 300 other people were wounded, some critically.

Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on Telegram that the attacks are in response to "brutal Saudi aggression against our country and our people," CBS News partner BBC News reported. He claimed Saudi Arabia launched more than 120 airstrikes in the past 24 hours in Houthi-controlled territory in Yemen.

The Houthis said their other targets included the Shugadam gas facility, which belongs to Saudi's national petroleum and natural gas company Aramco, the Tanajib oil refinery, and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, the BBC reported.
Saudi's civil aviation authority confirmed the strike on King Fahd Airport.

Saturday's strike at the airport, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, marked a major escalation in the war between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom and further complicated sputtering efforts to halt the

Saudi Arabia has moved Riyadh schools online amid the Houthis' latest threat. Flights were diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the U.S., Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport.
Earlier on Saturday, the Houthies threatened new attacks on the kingdom's airports, except for the holy sites of Mecca and Medina, warning passengers not to travel.
"The airports and airspace are exposed to targeting and constitute a theatre of operations for our forces," Saree wrote on X.
He urged "everyone to take our warnings seriously."
On Sunday, the Houthis said the airport under their control in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa had been struck again. They blamed the Saudis but provided no details.
The attack on Riyadh's airport on Saturday drew condemnation from the United Nations and world leaders, including President Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis.

"The United States strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis, including today's strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that took numerous innocent lives, including an American citizen," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a social media post.
A State Department spokesperson told CBS News the Trump administration is in close contact with its "Saudi partners."
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the attacks by Iran's proxies are "pushing the region into a spiral of violence."
"They are destabilizing crucial global transport and energy nodes," she wrote on X.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday condemned "in the strongest possible terms" the attack on King Khalid Airport and extended his condolences.

"Terrorism targets innocent people and seeks to spread fear and instability. It must be confronted with resolve," he said in a statement shared on X. "Israel looks forward to a strong Middle East—one that stands united against threats, protects its people, and builds a future of security, cooperation, and prosperity for all the peoples of our region.

The Saudi statement about Saturday's attack said the dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said several hospitals were treating the 309 people injured, some in serious condition.
The Egyptian woman was a flight attendant identified as Azza Ramzy, 28, who worked for the Saudi airline Flynas, according to the Egyptian state-run Al-Qahera News television.
The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said Sunday that one of its citizens died after being wounded in the attack on the Riyadh airport a day earlier.

"It is learnt that one Indian national injured in the Riyadh attack has unfortunately lost his life today. We convey our heartfelt condolences to the family of the deceased," the embassy wrote in a statement posted on X.
The Houthis claimed attacks earlier in the week on King Khalid International Airport that killed three Saudis, including a pilot. The airport has no military facilities.

The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis.

articles.headline: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
keyFacts: Microsoft President Brad Smith said global safety rules are needed because milk and washing machines are currently more regulated than AI.
Smith's position contrasts with President Donald Trump, who said the tech sector should regulate itself.
Smith stated that the United Kingdom is best placed to lead the development of global AI safety rules.
body: - Published
Milk and washing machines are currently more regulated than AI, the president of Microsoft has said.

Brad Smith said there needed to be global safety rules in place, including a legal obligation to tell a "victim" if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent as well as deciding when outside evaluators should sign off on an AI product before it is released.
His comments put him at odds with President Donald Trump, who said the sector should regulate itself so US firms don't lose out to Chinese rivals.
But Smith said: "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Demands for laws and rules to control AI have grown after experts in the sector said they believed the technology its a threat to humanity.
The bosses of the US-based AI giants such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind have all backed the idea of an AI development slowdown, but Trump has pushed against this.
Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview, Smith called AI both a "tool and a weapon" that urgently needed to be regulated.
"Let's get started today," he said.
He said firms need "emergency brakes" â often known in the industry as 'kill switches' â to pause or slowdown AI if it got out of control in some way.

He also said there should be a legal requirement for firms to write "incident reports" and tell victims if the technology goes rogue. He also suggested that independent government evaluators should vet new AI technology.
"We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI."

Smith said the UK was best placed to drive forward these global rules for AI because of its AI Security Institute, external, launched during former prime minister Rishi Sunak's government as the AI Safety Institute.

"In the world of technology, in the tech sector, most people that I know would say, if you ask them, name the country that is the leader in having this technical capability, they would say, it's very simple. It's the United Kingdom. They are the best."
'The moment has arrived'
Smith's views are very different to those of his president, who believes the US should be going full-steam ahead on AI.
Trump has repeatedly said that "whoever wins AI, wins".

However, Smith does not believe the US government would be as opposed to UK-led AI regulations as Trump's comments make it seem, suggesting the US would be more accepting of the UK making standards than the EU.
"In Washington DC, people don't look at the UK and they don't look at London the way they look at Brussels â that's a strength," he said.
"When you look at AI agents that have escaped human control, when you look at models that are so powerful that they're putting the world's cybersecurity at risk. I would say: The moment has arrived.
"Let's speak calmly, maybe even softly, but firmly, and start to bring people together. I hope that's the role we can play as a company. I hope that's the role the UK can play as a country."
At the end of last month, Trump hosted the leaders of US tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta, and Google at the White House where the executives signed a "morally binding" document.
The companies agreed to work with "independent auditors" to assess whether their AI systems are working as intended and make sure they do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways".
Smith said he applauds the statement and Microsoft is "happy to sign it".
"It's a good step, it's a necessary step... But I don't think it's sufficient any longer."
He added that the challenge for any "self-regulatory regime" is that "the good companies will do what you want".
"It's the companies that are not as responsible that you need to worry about."

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia: Second strike kills at least 1 at Riyadh airport
keyFacts: A strike on Riyadh airport killed one Pakistani national and injured 11 others on Sunday, Saudi authorities said.
Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for the attack and warned airlines against using Saudi airports and airspace.
The Saudi-led coalition vowed a tough response, while President Trump said the United States would look at joining strikes against the rebels.
body: At least one person was killed and 11 others were injured in a stike on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia on Sunday, a day after a similar attack killed 12 and injured hundreds.
"King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was subjected to a new attack on Sunday afternoon," the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement.
It later confirmed that the individual killed in the Sunday attack was a Pakistani national.

A spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen said that a cruise missile had been intercepted by air defense systems in the vicinity of the airport, but no further details were immediately available.
The Houthis later claimed responsibility for the strikes, saying they had "carried out four qualitative operations in the past 24 hours using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones."
A spokesman said the group targeted the Riyadh airport multiple times, as well as the Dammam airport in the east of the country and two facilities belonging to the Saudi state oil company Aramco.
Later on Sunday evening, Saudi authorities also confirmed an attack on Dammam airport.
Houthis warn airlines to avoid Saudi Arabia
The latest Houthi strikes also came just hours after the rebel group warned airlines and travelers to avoid Saudi airports.

"We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travelers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theater of operations for our forces," read a statement released by the group on social media. It added that airports in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina would not be targeted.
"We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously," the statement continued, stating: "Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions."
Why are Saudi airports being targeted?

Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the rebels seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month, including around the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

The Houthi-run health authority claimed this weekend that 91 Yemenis have been killed by the Saudi-led coalition in the last five weeks, 60% of them women and children. Earlier on Sunday, it said a child was killed and six people wounded in a suspected Saudi airstrike on a house in Sanaa.
The Houthi-run Al Masirah TV also reported that Saudi Arabia had struck the international airport in Sanaa on Sunday afternoon.
There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the claims.

"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the Houthi-run Foreign Ministry said in statements carried by Al Masirah TV on Sunday, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.
What has Saudi Arabia said about the Riyadh airport attacks?

The Saudi-led coalition, which supports the internationally recognized Yemeni government in its conflict against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels, vowed a tough response to the attack, which it labeled a "full-fledged war crime."
The Houthi strikes on Riyadh come amid a surge in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia this week, which have targeted other airports, military sites and oil infrastructure.
The spike in attacks has followed a major military offensive by the Saudi-led coalition against the Houthis.
The rebels, one of Tehran's regional proxies, have been fighting Yemen's government, which is recognized by the international community, since the outbreak of a civil war over a decade ago.

While a truce in 2022 froze the conflict, it failed to secure a lasting peace deal. The US-Israeli war with Iran has seen fighting flare up again in Yemen, worsening an already severe humanitarian crisis.
How has the international community reacted to the Riyadh strikes?
US President Donald Trump on Saturday said he would be speaking to Saudi Arabia's de facto leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, in the wake of the attack, which he said was "not acceptable."
Trump also said that the US was "going to look" at potentially joining Saudi strikes against the rebels.
On Sunday, European leaders expressed their "shock" at the attack on Riyadh airport.
The president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, said the EU stands in "solidarity with Saudi Arabia" as she condemned the "dangerous escalation."

"These attacks by Iran's proxies are pushing the region into a spiral of violence. They are destabilizing crucial global transport and energy nodes with shock waves sent through the world," von der Leyen said.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul "firmly" condemned what he described as "a terrorist act against Saudi Arabia and civil aviation".
"Our thoughts are with the victims and I send my sincere condolences to their loved ones," he said on X.

UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting slammed the attacks as "contemptible" and a "dangerous escalation," while the French Foreign Ministry condemned the "heinous attack" and stressed its "total solidarity" with Saudi Arabia.
Russia, which is a strategic partner of Iran, also condemned the Houthis' attack and called for the hostilities to end "through political and diplomatic means."
Australia, meanwhile, has urged its citizens in the Saudi capital to "shelter in place" amid the escalating attacks.

body: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle may soon be fired amid reports she sought a six-figure credit card bailout from a Trump donor while offering access to administration officials, adding to mounting allegations over her conduct in Athens.

President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are "extremely pissed off" by Guilfoyle’s reported conduct and are weighing her removal, The Associated Press reported Sunday, citing a senior U.S. official.
The official told the AP that a decision on what action to take would likely come this week after Monday’s Columbus Day holiday. No departure has been confirmed.

Guilfoyle, onetime fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., came under scrutiny this week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing.

According to messages reviewed by the Journal, Guilfoyle urged Deters to wire the money directly to American Express, saying the transaction would not leave a paper trail, while offering to help him gain access to senior Trump administration officials. Deters said he never made the payment.
Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages.

The allegations followed an earlier Journal investigation into Guilfoyle's conduct in Greece, including claims that she promoted the interests of Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group and allowed its registered lobbyist, Christos Marafatsos, to accompany her to private diplomatic meetings with senior officials.
FORMER TRUMP CABINET OFFICIAL HAD 'INAPPROPRIATELY CLOSE' RELATIONSHIP WITH BODYGUARD, IG FINDS

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle suggested at a dinner with Greek officials that the U.S. would undermine their government, citing political developments in Romania. Greece's foreign minister has since said there was no need to summon Guilfoyle for an explanation because the country's energy minister denied that any threat had been made.

Separately, the State Department 's Office of Inspector General opened an investigation into allegations involving Guilfoyle's treatment of embassy employees, private travel, acceptance of gifts and relationships with business interests, according to a report from the Daily Mail.
3 SECRET SERVICE OFFICIALS UNDER INTERNAL INVESTIGATION FOR POTENTIAL MISCONDUCT

Sources described a hostile workplace in which Guilfoyle allegedly threatened to fire employees. They also claim that she demoted members of her security detail over minor incidents, including an officer who reportedly failed to answer a 4 a.m. request for ice while she was vacationing in Mykonos.
The inspector general's office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation. Binnall told the Daily Mail that "any implication of wrongdoing by the Ambassador is unsupported."

The allegations have drawn scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., who have called for a review of Guilfoyle's conduct. Meeks urged her removal if the allegations were substantiated.
Vice President JD Vance addressed the controversy Friday, cautioning against rushing to judgment while acknowledging that misconduct should carry consequences.
OHIO BAKERY WORKERS RECOUNT SURPRISE JD VANCE ENCOUNTER THAT TOOK AN UNEXPECTED TURN

"Let's actually see what the facts are. Let's see what the truth is," Vance told reporters in Ohio. "And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it."
Secretary of State Marco Rubio , who visited Greece this week and delivered remarks with the backdrop of Acropolis, declined to address the allegations directly.
SEC MARCO RUBIO: THE WEST FORGOT WHAT MADE IT GREAT. WE MUST REDISCOVER OUR ROOTS BEFORE WE LOSE THEM
"You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel," Rubio told reporters Thursday.
Rubio had defended Guilfoyle's performance a day earlier, saying, "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here."
FOUR AMERICAN TOURISTS AMONG 6 KILLED AFTER EXPLOSION LEVELS BUILDING NEAR ATHENS’ ACROPOLIS

Trump nominated Guilfoyle to the diplomatic post in December 2024. A former California prosecutor and Fox News Channel personality, she previously served as a prominent surrogate and fundraiser for the president.

Guilfoyle was almost Trump’s daughter-in-law. She was engaged to Don Jr. for four years, but the two publicly split in Dec. 2024 — the same month the president nominated her to be the ambassador to Greece.
The president’s eldest son married Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson in May of this year.
She was also previously married to California Gov. Gavin Newsom , a Democrat, from 2001 to 2006, when he was serving as mayor of San Francisco.

articles.headline: 10 Best Episodes of 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' Of All Time, Ranked by Their IMDb Score
keyFacts: Polygon published a list ranking the top ten episodes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer based on their IMDb scores.
The episodes Hush, Once More with Feeling, and The Body earned the highest IMDb ratings on the list at 9.7.
The top-ranked episode Hush received two Emmy nominations for writing and cinematography, according to the article.
body: Despite premiering almost three decades ago, Buffy the Vampire Slayer still endures. This beloved supernatural show didn’t just lay the foundation for a strong, well-rounded female lead in Buffy Summers (Sarah Michelle Gellar). Buffy also subverted established horror tropes and consistently mastered the “monster-of-the-week” format in a way few shows could in the late '90s. Stigma and stereotypes were broken all the time. Buffy never treated femininity and world-altering strength as mutually exclusive.

A successful show that ran for seven seasons is bound to have exceptional episodes. Some are memorable because of the Big Bad featured in them, while others feature crucial character moments or exciting stakes. With these factors in mind, here are 10 best episodes of Buffy the Vampire Slayer of all time, according to their IMDb scores.
10 10. “Graduation Day: Part 2” (Season 3, Episode 22)
IMDb Rating: 9.1/10

This two-part season 3 finale is at its strongest when considered as a unit, but “Graduation Day: Part 2” is a satisfying conclusion to some major storylines. Buffy and the Scooby Gang aren’t alone in their fight against evil, as the entire school bands together to defeat Mayor Wilkins (Harry Groener) and his evil plot to become a giant demon and murder everyone in town. This episode is also a major turning point for Angel (David Boreanaz), who leaves Sunnydale after realizing he cannot provide Buffy with the normalcy that she deserves. “Part 2” takes the show’s “high school is hell” metaphor to its limits, where Buffy’s silent efforts as protector are finally validated.
9 9. “Fool for Love” (Season 5, Episode 7)
IMDb Rating: 9.1

A definite high point in the show, “Fool for Love” humanizes Spike (James Marsters), whose pre-vampire backstory as the shy, insecure poet William is revealed. We come to understand that vampirism doesn’t completely change a person, but amplifies their flaws in the most brutal ways. We’re also asked to question what we know about Slayers, as Spike posits that all Slayers have an unconscious death wish. Given the enormous responsibility that every Slayer needs to shoulder, they unwittingly embrace death after being burned out by their isolated lifestyles — at least according to the bleached-blond bloodsucker. Buffy is put under scrutiny here, but we’re also privy to some of the more vulnerable aspects of Spike, and his complicated relationship with the titular Slayer.
8 8. “Doppelgängland” (Season 3, Episode 16)
IMDb Rating: 9.2

What would happen in an alternate reality where Buffy never arrived to save Sunnydale? The series explores this terrifying thought experiment in an earlier season 3 episode, "The Wish," revealing a world where Willow and Xander aren't just evil vampires — they're also dating. Later that season, evil Willow gets transported into the show's main reality in “Doppelgängland,” arriving just in time to give regular old reliable Willow an unlikely confidence boost.

Alyson Hannigan delivers an electrifying dual performance, and a particularly amusing switcheroo scenario makes for a genuinely fun episode. Aside from these comedic moments, Willow must confront the darker aspects of her personality, and accept them to an extent without losing who she truly is.
7 7. “Passion” (Season 2, Episode 17)
IMDb Rating: 9.3

Despite his sincerely well-meaning actions throughout the first season, Angel has always felt like a benign threat due to his vampiric nature. In season 2, that threat becomes the primary focus after Buffy and Angel sleep together, inadvertently undoing the curse that gave the vampire a soul.

A few episodes later, Buffy raises the stakes even further in “Passion” as Angel's soulless alter ego Angelus begins to actively go on the offensive via psychological torture and mass murder. This adds a genuinely terrifying edge to Buffy’s feelings for Angel, and how these emotions morph once Angelus starts tormenting Buffy and her loved ones. The episode also features a shocking death, pushing everyone, including the level-headed Giles, into the pits of despair. Buffy has always dabbled in mature themes, but this particular episode fully embraces the moral complexities of what it means to be a monster.
6 6. "Chosen" (Season 7, Episode 22)
IMDb Rating: 9.3

Buffy's seventh and final season is nobody's favorite, but the series finale episode is still an all-time classic that manages to give pretty much every character a fitting sendoff. (Except Anya, R.I.P.)

The finale's smartest twist is a plan that turns the entire show's premise on its head. Being a Slayer comes with an inevitable sense of isolation. “Chosen” radically changes the status quo by allowing Buffy to share the burden with every potential Slayer, whose powers get activated thanks to Willow's spell. This Slayer activation spell is a literal game-changer, as it puts an end to unnecessary tragedy and rewrites the rules of what it means to be a protector. Buffy has effectively undergone major transformations since the show began, but she is a mature, strategic leader in “Chosen.” Spike also gets his big redemption moment and shares an extremely bittersweet moment with Buffy. Despite these setbacks, the underlying sentiment is hope for the future. Nobody has to suffer alone, as power can now be democratized instead of being sustained by one person.
5 5. “The Gift” (Season 5, Episode 22)
IMDb Rating: 9.5

Buffy's brilliant season 5 finale is particularly devastating. The fate of Dawn (a mystical key transformed into Buffy's sister for protection) becomes the point of contention, but Buffy protectively steps in, as she refuses to view Dawn as a necessary sacrifice. Instead, Buffy sacrifices her own life and dives into a dimensional portal in Dawn's place. There’s an emotional finality to this selfless act, as it underlines Buffy’s growth from a reluctant teenager to an adult who makes the most difficult choice to keep everyone safe. This is a bleak, tragic end to a relentlessly courageous soul — even if she managed to come back from the dead at the start of season 6.
4 4. “Becoming: Part 2” (Season 2, Episode 22)
IMDb Rating: 9.5

Yet another wonderful season finale, “Becoming: Part 2” is a high point for Buffy as a character. She goes through a lot after becoming a fugitive and making an unlikely alliance with Spike, but her confrontation with Angelus takes on new meaning. This is also the episode where Buffy blocks Angelus’ swords with her bare hands. “No weapons, no friends, no hope. Take all that away, and what is left?” he taunts, to which Buffy replies, “Me.” This finale ends in heartbreak for Buffy, while Willow is able to achieve a significant milestone in her journey to becoming a powerful witch.
3 3. “The Body” (Season 5, Episode 16)
IMDb Rating: 9.7
One of the best Buffy episodes of all time isn't about a monster at all. When Buffy's mom, Joyce, dies, it's not because of a demon attack or a vampire bite. Instead, it's a brain aneurysm.

Buffy returns home to find her mom lying lifeless on the couch, and becomes completely unmoored by this grief. There’s no supernatural intervention or melodrama here — everyone is forced to sit with the reality of death. Numbness grips Buffy, while Xander and Willow process it outwardly, being prone to frustrated outbursts. All of these reactions are valid, and the episode does a beautiful job of depicting the unvarnished shock of loss. Gellar, who usually relies on animated expressions to convey Buffy’s nuances, delivers an appropriately restrained performance that hits really hard.
2 2. “Once More, with Feeling” (Season 6, Episode 7)
IMDb Rating: 9.7

One would think that a one-off musical episode in Buffy would be a fun, throwaway gimmick, but “Once More, with Feeling” makes excellent use of the format. Major reveals become a part of song and dance, specifically related to Buffy’s death at the end of season 5 and her return at the start of this season. The far-reaching implications are allowed to fester, as every character inadvertently learns the truth during this episode. The songs in question are also well-penned, shifting genres as per moods, such as when Xander and Anya (Emma Caulfield) perform a 1950s-style song to talk about the doubts in their relationship. It is tricky for a show like Buffy to use musicals as a vehicle to further character motivations, but this episode does so with great confidence.
1 1. “Hush” (Season 4, Episode 10)
IMDb Rating: 9.7

Easily one of the most inventive episodes in television history, “Hush” relies on visual storytelling instead of the show’s characteristic witty banter. The long stretches of silence work in favor of character growth. Everyone is forced to communicate with silent cues and gestures, making it more difficult to keep their defenses up. The episode also features some chilling antagonists, who essentially steal everyone’s voices in Sunnydale to carry out their sinister schemes. Apart from some significant romantic developments that occur here, the episode is a good reminder that Buffy doesn’t always need spectacle to shine. “Hush” won two Emmy nominations for Outstanding Writing in a Drama Series and Outstanding Cinematography, which speaks to its exceptional quality.

articles.headline: Jesse Lingard gets four-time Champions League winner as new manager at Brazilian club

body: Clarence Seedorf has landed his first managerial job in seven years by becoming the new head coach at Corinthians.
Seedorf, who won four Champions League titles at Ajax, Real Madrid and AC Milan, is eyed as one of football’s greatest-ever midfielders.
Seedorf has returned to management by taking the head coach role at Corinthians, seven years after his last job Getty
He also won 87 caps for the Netherlands national team and played at the 1998 World Cup.
After his retirement in 2014, Seedorf managed Milan, Shenzhen FC and Deportivo La Coruna.
A spell at Cameroon followed but ended in 2019, with Brazilian outfit Corinthians the 50-year-old’s next challenge.
Seedorf has signed a deal with the club until the end of next year.
Corinthians have slipped to 17th in the 2026 Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A table and are now in the relegation zone following a heavy defeat to league leaders Palmeiras on Sunday evening.
However, they won the Supercopa do Brasil earlier in the year with a 2-0 win over Flamengo.
Lingard set for new Corinthians manager
Many fans of English football will recognise one of the players in Jesse Lingard, who signed for the club in March.
The former Manchester United and West Ham United star moved to Brazil after terminating his contract with FC Seoul in South Korea.
Lingard was an FA Cup, League Cup and Europa League winner with United, and made 182 appearances in the Premier League .
Now at Corinthians, the 33-year-old attacking midfielder has scored two goals and assisted one other in 29 outings.
Lingard is a regular for Corinthians, who are the ninth club of his playing career Getty
His first goal for the club, their winner against Barra in the Copa do Brasil, meant he became the only English scorer in the competition .
Lingard then found the target in a 2-0 Copa Libertadores victory over Penarol.
Corinthians last played on Wednesday night but were beaten 2-1 by Internacional in the league, with Lingard an unused substitute.
Now with Seedorf in charge, the seven-time Brazilian champions will hope to salvage their season before it ends in December.
“Taking on this challenge is an honour, but also a huge responsibility,” their new head coach said upon his arrival.
“I am here to give my all and build a team that fights for every ball, every minute, every victory.”

articles.headline: Barrasso predicts Guilfoyle inquiry amid reports of White House tension
keyFacts: Sen. John Barrasso said he believes U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle will be investigated following reports alleging ethics violations.
A senior official said President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are considering firing Guilfoyle over the allegations.
Barrasso anticipates the State Department and the Senate Foreign Relations Committee will conduct oversight inquiries into Guilfoyle.
body: Sen. John Barrasso (R-WY) said on Sunday he believes U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle will be investigated following a series of reports alleging ethics violations.

While speaking with Margaret Brennan on Face the Nation , Barrasso was asked whether there might be an investigation, such as an inquiry by the Department of State Office of Inspector General, into questions surrounding her conduct in office. A series of three Wall Street Journal reports released in recent weeks outline allegations that she tapped a Trumpworld ally to pay off $100,000 in credit card debt and that Greek businessmen have paid for luxurious travel arrangements.

A member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Barrasso said he cannot confirm an investigation is underway, but he believes one may happen. President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are considering firing Guilfoyle and are “extremely pissed off” by the alleged conduct, a senior U.S. official told the Associated Press on Sunday.

“What we’ve seen in the reports is very troubling, it’s concerning, and I’m sure there’s going to be an investigation,” Barrasso said. “I would assume the State Department would be conducting that, I know that the Senate Foreign Relations Committee will have oversight and look into that as well. But I think the public has a right to know what is found, and it is quite a bit of concern.”

When asked if he’s comfortable with U.S. officials’ debts being paid off in exchange for political access, Barrasso said he’s not, but he’s currently focused on campaigning for Republican candidates ahead of November’s midterm elections. Reports indicate Democrats are likely to investigate Trump administration officials’ business ties if they retake the House of Representatives in November to lay the groundwork for potential articles of impeachment.

“You know, we’re going to be back after the elections,” he said, “but for the next three weeks we are going to be campaigning across the country, and I’m sure we’ll discuss that later, but the focus today is making sure the American people know just how far left the Democrats have gone.”
RUBIO LASHES OUT AT MEDIA FOR DEMANDING COMMENT ON GUILFOYLE REPORT

Rubio brushed aside concerns about Guilfoyle while speaking to reporters in Athens on Wednesday, saying the “embassy here is doing a great job” and that reports should not be treated like evidence of guilt. Rubio delivered an address in front of the Acropolis during his three-country European tour that received widespread praise from Republicans.

Guilfoyle, 57, broke a multiyear engagement to Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., in 2024. She was previously married to Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) and has worked as a Fox News host and prosecutor. She was confirmed as ambassador to Greece in September 2025.

articles.headline: GTA 6 Leaker Posts Grainy Footage Of Lucia Skydiving Naked To Sell Crypto
keyFacts: The user Cyberleek posted leaked footage of GTA 6 protagonist Lucia naked to promote a cryptocurrency scheme.
Cyberleek claimed they will release a playable build of GTA 6 if their cryptocurrency reaches a $30 million market cap.
Cyberleek claimed publisher Take-Two could avoid the release by distributing a disc version of GTA 6 and apologizing to players.
body: After going quiet for over a month following the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended reveal on Netflix, the account Cyberleek has been busy over the last few days with fresh gameplay leaks and threats. The unknown user claimed they would release a playable build of the game if their crypto meme coin hit a $30 million market cap, and they’re now posting footage of Lucia naked to try to drive up the price.

The latest leak shows the game’s female lead driving around the city, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and visiting an ATM. It also spends a significant amount of time with the Parachuting side mission and mini-games teased in the previous gameplay reveal. The footage also looks janky in parts, leaving viewers to wonder just how old the build it’s from is.market cap

The latest Lucia footage comes as the leaker polls people online for what should be released next. They’re promising to release longer and more detailed versions of “naked Lucia” the more people buy into their crypto scheme.
Cyberleek reveals that he has access to Lucia fully naked in GTA 6, and will publish the footage depending on his tokenâs marketcap.
Heâs using this tactic to manipulate people into his pump-and-dump crypto scheme again, so beware. pic.twitter.com/6q0PmoVOIA
— GTA 6 Countdown â³ (@GTAVI_Countdown) October 10, 2026

The existing theory is that Cyberleek is using some sort of older build or debug mode to show off the game’s two protagonists without any clothes on, and that it’s unclear if this is a thing that can happen in the actual story campaign itself. Bystanders in the world don’t react to Lucia being naked in the latest leak, suggesting something else is indeed going on.

Whatever the account has access to, it’s threatening to release it if enough people buy its $Cyberleek meme coin. It’s currently at a market cap of around $4.75 million, up significantly since the leaker’s apparent return. But that’s still a very long way from $30 million. The account has also claimed that Take-Two can avoid a threatened release of some version of GTA 6 if it releases a disc version of the game and “apologizes” to players.

Any semblance of some pro-consumer stance has been undercut by the preparation for another attempt at a crypto rug pull. The last time Cyberleek went quiet, the account seemingly made off with roughly $250,000 in dumped crypto. With just over a month until GTA 6’s release, it’s not gunning for a much bigger payday.

body: Apple will announce a new smart home hub on Tuesday called the HomeView, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.

Over the past couple of years, we’ve seen multiple reports that Apple was working on a new smart home product, but now it seems the product has a name and a launch date. Gurman described the HomeView as a Siri-powered device with a display and an A18 chip, allowing customers to control their other smart home devices.

articles.headline: A college in Illinois tried to cancel its Flock contact and it refused
keyFacts: In October 2025, Elgin Community College asked Flock to remove its safety cameras over data privacy and security concerns.
Flock refused the removal requests and ignored a later offer from school officials to pay for the remaining contract months.
College staff repeatedly covered the cameras with trash bags, but workers assumed to be from Flock kept removing the covers until the contract expired.
body: In April of 2025, Elgin Community College had six Flock safety cameras installed to “enhance the safety and security of students.” But by September of that year, the school’s administration grew concerned that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not properly secured, and that both law enforcement and the company’s employees were abusing access to the data.
A college in Illinois tried to cancel its Flock contact and it refused
Flock refused to take its cameras down so Elgin Community College covered them. The company snuck back to undue it.

So in October of 2025, Elgin Community College requested Flock to remove its cameras. According to Elgin’s President Peggy Heinrich, Flock rejected the request, saying it had not violated its contract. According to the Chicago Sun-Times, school officials reached out again in December, offered to pay for the remaining five months of the contract, and still requested that the cameras be removed. They were met with silence.

Heinrich said Elgin Community College staff began to cover the cameras using black trash bags and zip ties so that they would not be able to capture footage. But workers in an unmarked vehicle, which Heinrich assumed belonged to Flock, repeatedly removed the coverings.
“We were kind of in a back and forth for a bit where we’d cover, and then when they’d come to service, they’d remove,” Heinrich said. “Then we’d cover and then they’d remove.”
This continued until April of this year when the college’s contract expired, and Flock removed the cameras.
